questions.knowledge_point: Computing Coefficients in a Partial Fractions Decomposition
questions.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{x+4}{({x}^{2}+4)x}=\frac{-x+B}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x},
$$

what is the value of $B?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+4)x$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x+4 & =(-x+B)x+({x}^{2}+4).\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)+4 & =(-1+B)(1)+({1}^{2}+4) \\ 5 & =-1+B+5 \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+5}{({x}^{2}+2)(x-1)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+2}+\frac{2}{x-1},
$$

what is the value of $B?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+2)(x-1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-3x+5 & =(2x+B)(x-1)+2({x}^{2}+2).\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}-3(0)+5 & =(2(0)+B)(0-1)+2({0}^{2}+2) \\ 5 & =(B)(-1)+2(2) \\ 5 & =-B+4 \\ 1 & =-B \\ B & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$, $B$, and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{({x}^{2}+4)(x+2)}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{C}{x+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $({x}^{2}+4)(x+2)$ gives

$$
5=(Ax+B)(x+2)+C({x}^{2}+4).
$$

For $x=-2$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =C(4+4) \\ 5 & =8C \\ C & =\frac{5}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=0$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =(A(0)+B)(0+2)+\frac{5}{8}((0)^{2}+4) \\ 5 & =2B+\frac{5}{2} \\ 2B & =\frac{5}{2} \\ B & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=1$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =(A(1)+\frac{5}{4})(1+2)+\frac{5}{8}((1)^{2}+4) \\ 5 & =3A+\frac{15}{4}+\frac{25}{8} \\ 3A & =-\frac{15}{8} \\ A & =-\frac{5}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{({x}^{2}+4)(x+2)} & =\frac{(-\frac{5}{8}x+\frac{5}{4})}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{(\frac{5}{8})}{x+2} \\  & =\frac{-5\,x+10}{8({x}^{2}+4)}+\frac{5}{8(x+2)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{7x}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{C}{x-2},
$$

where $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A+B+C.$
questions.worked_solution:
We multiply both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)$ and get

$$
7x=(Ax+B)(x-2)+C({x}^{2}+3).
$$

Plugging in $x=2$ eliminates the $A$ and $B$ terms and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}7(2) & =(A(2)+B)(2-2)+C({2}^{2}+3) \\ 14 & =7C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}7(0) & =(A(0)+B)(0-2)+(2)({0}^{2}+3) \\ 0 & =-2B+6 \\ 2B & =6 \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}7(1) & =(A(1)+3)(1-2)+(2)({1}^{2}+3) \\ 7 & =(A+3)(-1)+8 \\ 7 & =-A+5 \\ A & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=-2,$ $B=3,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
A+B+C=-2+3+2=3.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{43{x}^{2}+4x+2}{(6{x}^{2}+1)(x-1)}=\frac{x+B}{6{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{7}{x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(6{x}^{2}+1)(x-1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}43{x}^{2}+4x+2 & =(x+B)(x-1)+7(6{x}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=0$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}43(0)^{2}+4(0)+2 & =(0+B)(0-1)+7(6(0)^{2}+1) \\ 2 & =-B+7 \\ B & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\frac{43{x}^{2}+4x+2}{(6{x}^{2}+1)(x-1)}=\frac{x+5}{6{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{7}{x-1}
$$

questions.problem: Express $\frac{7{x}^{2}-28x+17}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-5)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B$ and $C$ such that

$$
\frac{7{x}^{2}-28x+17}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-5)}=\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+1)}+\frac{C}{(x-5)}.
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+1$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+1)(x-5)$ and get

$$
7{x}^{2}-28x+17=(Ax+B)(x-5)+C({x}^{2}+1).
$$

Plugging in $x=5$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}7(5)^{2}-28(5)+17 & =(A(5)+B)(5-5)+C({5}^{2}+1) \\ 175-140+17 & =26C \\ 52 & =26C \\ C & =\frac{52}{26} \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}7(0)^{2}-28(0)+17 & =(A(0)+B)(0-5)+C({0}^{2}+1) \\ 17 & =-5B+C \\ 17 & =-5B+2 \\ 5B & =2-17 \\ B & =-\frac{15}{5} \\ B & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}7(1)^{2}-28(1)+17 & =(A(1)+B)(1-5)+C({1}^{2}+1) \\ -4 & =-4A-4B+2C \\ -4 & =-4A-4(-3)+2(2) \\ 4A & =12+4+4 \\ A & =\frac{20}{4} \\ A & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=5,$ $B=-3,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{7{x}^{2}-28x+17}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-5)}=\frac{5x-3}{({x}^{2}+1)}+\frac{2}{(x-5)}.
$$

questions.problem: Express $\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x-3}{({x}^{2}+6)(x+5)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x-3}{({x}^{2}+6)(x+5)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+6)}+\frac{C}{(x+5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+6$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+6)(x+5)$ and get

$$
3{x}^{2}+2x-3=(Ax+B)(x+5)+C({x}^{2}+6).
$$

Plugging in $x=-5$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-5)^{2}+2(-5)-3 & =(A(-5)+B)(-5+5)+C((-5)^{2}+6) \\ 75-10-3 & =31C \\ C & =\frac{62}{31} \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(0)^{2}+2(0)-3 & =(A(0)+B)(0+5)+C((0)^{2}+6) \\ -3 & =5B+6C \\ -3 & =5B+6(2) \\ 5B & =-3-12 \\ B & =\frac{-15}{5} \\ B & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A$ we choose $x=1$, and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}+2(1)-3 & =(A(1)+B)(1+5)+C((1)^{2}+6) \\ 2 & =6A+6B+7C \\ 2 & =6A+6(-3)+7(2) \\ 6A & =2+18-14 \\ A & =\frac{6}{6} \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=1,B=-3,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x-3}{({x}^{2}+6)(x+5)}=\frac{x-3}{({x}^{2}+6)}+\frac{2}{(x+5)}.
$$

questions.problem: Express $\frac{3{x}^{2}-3x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}-3x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)}=\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+3)}+\frac{C}{(x-2)}.
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+3$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)$ and get

$$
3{x}^{2}-3x+1=(Ax+B)(x-2)+C({x}^{2}+3).
$$

Plugging in $x=2$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(2)^{2}-3(2)+1 & =(A(2)+B)(2-2)+C({2}^{2}+3) \\ 12-6+1 & =7C \\ C & =\frac{7}{7} \\ C & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(0)^{2}-3(0)+1 & =(A(0)+B)(0-2)+C({0}^{2}+3) \\ 1 & =-2B+3C \\ 1 & =-2B+3(1) \\ 2B & =2 \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}-3(1)+1 & =(A(1)+B)(1-2)+C({1}^{2}+3) \\ 1 & =-A-B+4C \\ 1 & =-A-1+4(1) \\ A & =3-1 \\ A & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=2,$ $B=1$ and $C=1.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}-3x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)}=\frac{2x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)}+\frac{1}{(x-2)}.
$$

questions.problem: Express $\frac{2{x}^{2}+7x-1}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2{x}^{2}+7x-1}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)}+\frac{C}{(x+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}-2x+3$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)$ and get

$$
2{x}^{2}+7x-1=(Ax+B)(x+1)+C({x}^{2}-2x+3).
$$

Plugging in $x=-1$ eliminates the $A$ and $B$ terms and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-1)^{2}+7(-1)-1 & =(A(-1)+B)(-1+1)+C((-1)^{2}-2(-1)+3) \\ -6 & =6C \\ C & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)^{2}+7(0)-1 & =(A(0)+B)(0+1)+C({0}^{2}-2(0)+3) \\ -1 & =B+3C \\ -1 & =B+3(-1) \\ B & =3-1 \\ B & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(1)^{2}+7(1)-1 & =(A(1)+B)(1+1)+C((1)^{2}-2(1)+3) \\ 8 & =2A+2B+2C \\ 8 & =2A+2(2)+2(-1) \\ 2A & =8-4+2 \\ A & =\frac{6}{2} \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=3,B=2,$ and $C=-1.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{2{x}^{2}+7x-1}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)}=\frac{3x+2}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)}-\frac{1}{(x+1)}.
$$

questions.problem: Express $\frac{7{x}^{2}-18x+16}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-6)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7{x}^{2}-18x+16}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-6)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+4)}+\frac{C}{(x-6)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+4$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+4)(x-6)$ and get

$$
7{x}^{2}-18x+16=(Ax+B)(x-6)+C({x}^{2}+4).
$$

Plugging in $x=6$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}7(6)^{2}-18(6)+16 & =(A(6)+B)(6-6)+C({6}^{2}+4) \\ 252-108+16 & =40C \\ C & =\frac{160}{40} \\ C & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}7(0)^{2}-18(0)+16 & =(A(0)+B)(0-6)+C({0}^{2}+4) \\ 16 & =-6B+4C \\ 16 & =-6B+4(4) \\ 6B & =16-16 \\ B & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}7(1)^{2}-18(1)+16 & =(A(1)+B)(1-6)+C({1}^{2}+4) \\ 5 & =-5A-5B+5C \\ 5 & =-5A-5(0)+5(4) \\ 5A & =20-5 \\ A & =\frac{15}{5} \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=3,$ $B=0,$ and $C=4.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{7{x}^{2}-18x+16}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-6)}=\frac{3x}{({x}^{2}+4)}+\frac{4}{(x-6)}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that 

$$
\dfrac{7 x^2 - 2x - 13 }{(x^2+1)(x+1) } = \dfrac{9x+B}{ x^2 +1} - \dfrac{2}{x+1} ,
$$

what is the value of $B?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x^2+1)(x+1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}7{x}^{2}-2x-13 & =(9x+B)(x+1)-2({x}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}7(0)^{2}-2(0)-13 & =(9\cdot (0)+B)(0+1)-2((0)^{2}+1) \\ -13 & =B-2 \\ B & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Express $\dfrac{2x+3}{(x^2+4)(x-1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{C}{x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since $x^2+4$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $(x^2+4)(x-1)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+3 & =(Ax+B)(x-1)+C({x}^{2}+4).\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=1$ eliminates the $A$ and $B$ terms and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(1)+3 & =(A(1)+B)(1-1)+C({1}^{2}+4) \\ 5 & =5C \\ C & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)+3 & =(A(0)+B)(0-1)+C({0}^{2}+4) \\ 3 & =-B+4C \\ 3 & =-B+4(1) \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=2$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(2)+3 & =(A(2)+B)(2-1)+C({2}^{2}+4) \\ 7 & =2A+B+8C \\ 7 & =2A+1+8(1) \\ 2A & =-2 \\ A & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=-1,$ $B=1,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\dfrac{2x+3}{(x^2+4)(x-1)} = \dfrac{1-x}{x^2+4} +\dfrac{1}{x-1}.
$$
